t: What Cursor Is: The AI-First Code Editor
title: What Cursor Is: The AI-First Code Editor
description: Cursor is an AI-first code editor — a fork of VS Code — built around AI pair programming: Tab completions, Cmd+K inline edits, codebase-wide chat, and agent mode that writes multi-file changes. For AI developers it collapses the write-debug loop: describe the training script, get working code, iterate in chat. It looks like VS Code because it is VS Code, AI-native.

t: Tab Completion and Cmd+K: The Core Loop
title: Tab Completion and Cmd+K: The Core Loop
description: Tab accepts ghost-text completions as you type — often whole functions from a comment. Cmd+K (Ctrl+K) opens inline edit: select code, describe the change ('vectorize this loop'), and the edit applies in place. The core loop is type-comment-tab, select-describe-apply: the AI handles boilerplate while you handle intent.

print("Tab: accept ghost completions (comment -> whole function).")
print("Cmd+K: select code, describe change, applied in place.")
print("Loop: type-comment-TAB, select-describe-APPLY. You: intent. AI: boilerplate.")

t: Use Case: Debugging With the AI
title: Use Case: Debugging With the AI
description: Paste the traceback (or let Cursor see it), describe the symptom, and iterate: the AI suggests fixes with explanations, you apply and test. It shines on shape mismatches, CUDA errors, and API misuse — the errors with known patterns. It cannot run your GPU, so verify every fix by running: the loop is suggest-apply-RUN.

description: Cursor indexes your codebase for the @-codebase feature — understand the privacy modes: code snippets go to the AI provider in normal mode; privacy mode promises no training on your code and no retention. For proprietary AI work, know your mode and your company's policy before indexing the crown jewels. The setting matters more than the feature.

title: Prompting Discipline for Code AI
description: Good prompts are specific: the goal, the constraints (versions, interfaces), the acceptance ('must handle empty batches'). Bad prompts are wishes ('make it better'). Include the error text for bugs, the shape for tensor code, the schema for data code. The AI is only as precise as the prompt — discipline in, quality out.

demo.program:
print("Good: goal + constraints (versions/interfaces) + acceptance criteria.")
print("Bad: 'make it better'. Bugs: include error text. Tensors: include shapes.")
print("AI precision = prompt precision. Discipline in, quality out.")

title: Verifying AI-Written Code
description: Every AI-written line gets the same verification as human code: run it, test edge cases, read the diff for subtle wrongness (off-by-ones, device mismatches, silent dtype casts). AI code fails most often at boundaries — empty inputs, GPU/CPU transitions, version differences. Trust the speedup, verify the output: the discipline that makes AI coding safe.

demo.program:
print("Verify like human code: RUN it, edge cases, read diffs for subtle wrongness.")
print("AI fails at boundaries: empty inputs, device transitions, version drift.")
print("Trust the speedup, VERIFY the output.")
